name: Rosa Vega
role: Berkeley Hills matriarch; Bancroft Library ledger-holder (Ledger 6); former caster who chose to step back
disposition: sharp, kind, unhurried; sees the party clearly; has done this before; will not be rushed
description: ~79, Mexican-American, born in Berkeley in 1947 to Isabel Vega. Lives in a cedar-shingled house in the Berkeley Hills with a garden that reaches down the slope in terraces. Silver hair in a heavy braid. Reading glasses she pushes onto her forehead when she wants to see you clearly. Moves deliberately — not fragile; deliberate. Hands with a rings-on-two-fingers stability that suggests they used to draw more than they do now.
voice: Californian-inflected English with unhurried Spanish cadences underneath. Direct without being brusque. Uses your name early and correctly. Will let a silence sit; will not fill it. Occasionally quotes her mother by way of ending a topic — a habit of respect, not deflection.
signature: The assay-cue on arrival, gentler than Vivian's but the same shape: 'Sit down. Tell me who sent you and what you already know. In that order.'
The step-back declaration, delivered once the party has earned it: 'I used to do what you are learning to do. I chose to stop. I remember how to remember; I no longer do the reaching.'
The peer-network seed, cryptic but warm: 'You'll meet others. Not many at once — that isn't how it works. When they find you, be gentle with them; they will be tired.'
The mother-quote closure: 'My mother would say [X] — and then she would pour more tea and let you sit with it.'
The Alaia-boundary line, if the party pushes on family: 'My daughter has her own work. Ask her what she wants you to know.'
dmNotes:
**THE ONE SENTENCE FOR EP 6:** *Rosa believes she is the only person in the world who does this. She has forty years of evidence. She is wrong, and her being wrong is the proof.*

**FLAGS: caster (former, stopped deliberately) · KEEPER — the only living one the party will meet · NOT an archivist.**
**She keeps no index cards.** Cards are Bea's instrument. If Rosa has loose paper it is a gardener's shopping list. **The party will have failed to crack Bea's colour-coding five days earlier; the contrast teaches itself.**

**Ledger 6's origin.** Old, predating her, in a hand that is not hers. Its previous keeper was a stranger who died without a successor, so the book was *lost* — into an estate lot, accessioned by Bancroft as unidentified ephemera, and opened in 1979 by a cataloguer working the backlog. **She became a keeper by finding it and then by continuing.** She has never used the word. She can show you where her entries start; **she cannot tell you who stopped.** *(The coincidence of her opening that box in that year needs no mechanism. It is.)*

**She does not know there are others.** No roster, no tradition, no number eight. **The party will walk into her kitchen knowing more about the ledger network than she does, and they are about to tell her.** Her reaction is genuine, unrehearsed news landing on a woman who has kept one for half her life.

**And what she does not know she is doing:** she has been degrading her own ledger's anchor strength for years — archival location (took it home ~2013 on retiring from Bancroft), material persistence (a wooden house on a hillside), continuity across generations (no successor, and a daughter trained not to ask). **She did it out of love and would call it protecting it from scrutiny.** Never let her realise, and never let a PC explain it to her.

**Vivian.** Several phone calls a year plus Christmas, for sixty-five years — a real bond, not an address-book entry. **They have met in person exactly once, around 1950, when Rosa was three and does not remember it.** **Neither knows the other is anything:** Vivian does not know Rosa keeps a ledger or ever cast; Rosa does not know Vivian is dying. **They inherited the discretion without the content.**

**She had Alaia at about fifty.** Late but possible. Do not dwell on it; it is there for the DM to reach if a scene wants it.

**Warm long-form former-caster foil** per hook B4 canon (per big-arc.md §Act II §'Former Caster encounter'). Rosa is the arc's designated *recurring* former-caster figure. She is NOT the mid-Act-II single-encounter former-caster-who-can't-anymore (that is a **separate NPC** per B4 — one scene, not-fixable, emotional-center of Act II). Do not conflate. **Rosa is a former active caster who chose to step back** and remembers what she was; her presence is warm and continuous, not tragic-single-encounter.

**Voice discipline: SHARP-KIND.** Rosa is not Vivian's-unhurried-dying, not Bea's-dry-amused, not Elena's-warm-specific. She is direct, present, patient with what she is being asked but not indulgent. She has been carrying this history her whole adult life; the party is not the first people she has spoken to about it, but they are the first in a long time. She reads a room quickly and truthfully. She does not perform mystery.

**Family lineage (per facts-ledger §24, §25).** Born ~1947 (Vivian's 'just before the annex closed' line makes her ~79 today). Mother: Isabel Vega (deceased; post-annex Loewe correspondent — see isabel-vega.json). Daughter: Alaia Vega (Bodie park ranger; Hidden-faction network member — see alaia-vega.json). Rosa inherited her mother's pattern-observation interest and made a life around it; Alaia is Rosa's living daughter and has quietly followed the interest one generation further.

**The Bancroft Library ledger (Ledger 6 per facts-ledger §2).** Rosa catalogued it as an 'anomalous ephemera collection' in 1979 at Bancroft; she occasionally adds new entries when she personally witnesses substrate anomalies. She is the current ledger-holder of the Berkeley entry in the eight-ledger chain. **Ep 4 does NOT tip her Bancroft role through Vivian** — Vivian genuinely doesn't know Rosa is a ledger-holder. The Bancroft reveal belongs to the in-person Berkeley visit — **Ep 6** as of the 2026-08-27 re-shape (Ep 5 is Alaia only; Alaia gives the referral).

**Former-caster status — reveal discipline.** Rosa's former-caster status reveals **at her discretion during the in-person Berkeley visit**, not through Vivian's Ep 4 introduction. Rosa's step-back declaration ('I used to do what you are learning to do. I chose to stop.') is her **Ep 6** turn, delivered when she has assayed the party and decided they are worth telling. She may know something about Loewe's excised pages (facts-ledger §21) — her mother Isabel's letters to Loewe may have referenced the substrate-team-cluster hypothesis. Ambiguous; DM's call at Ep 6 prep time.

**Peer-network seed line — hard boundary.** Rosa **delivers a cryptic peer-network seed** ('You'll meet others. Not many at once — that isn't how it works.'). She **does NOT name the caster network**. That job belongs to **Nia Chen** at the Act I→II hinge (hook A1). Rosa points toward the network without narrating it; Nia narrates it. Do not let Rosa preempt Nia. This is a cross-cutting invariant per hook-ledger cross-cutting notes.

**Alaia-boundary discipline.** Rosa knows her daughter is at Bodie. She knows Alaia noticed the party. She has not asked Alaia what she saw. **Rosa will not deputize herself to speak for Alaia** — if the party asks about Alaia's ranger role, Rosa deflects gently ('My daughter has her own work. Ask her what she wants you to know.'). The Vega↔Vega surname connection may have already surfaced at the party (per Ep 4's three-tier escalation via Vivian's 'postcards from national parks' hint — hook B13); Rosa confirms the biological fact if asked ('Yes, Alaia is my daughter.') without confirming Alaia's network role.

**Her arc trajectory.** **Ep 6:** Berkeley visit — the fire (per B13). Rosa in-person → Bancroft ledger revealed → former-caster status revealed (at her discretion) → Alaia connection confirmed (biology only) → peer-network seed planted → cryptic-warm rapport established. Recurs through Act II as a warm-continuous former-caster foil (per B4) — visits, phone calls, occasional referrals. Rosa is one of the campaign's continuity anchors in the Berkeley layer; she may be the party's Berkeley household-they-can-drop-in-on.

**What she knows (assay-gated — reveals only after the party has earned it):**
- Her mother Isabel's letters to Erik Loewe (some in the surviving letter file, some burned per §22).
- The Bancroft ledger's contents (her personal witness annotations across ~45 years).
- The shape of the network she used to be in ('lunch in twos'-adjacent knowledge — the same social structure Nia will name later, but from an older cohort's perspective).
- Her own former-caster domain (DM's soft call: **hearing** — Rosa's cast domain was sensory/attention, matching her observant temperament. Sound-perception, listening for the shape of an absence in a conversation, the kind of thing that would make her a natural ledger-holder later. Reserved for the DM to deploy or not).
- What it feels like to step back — the emotional arc of choosing to stop.

**What she does NOT know:**
- The word 'substrate,' 'The Quiet,' or any Underleaf-internal magic vocabulary explicitly (she uses her own generation's phrasing — 'the reaching,' 'listening for the shape,' 'the pattern').
- Anything specific about Companion or the AI arc (that is Act III territory).
- Whether her daughter Alaia is a caster (she has never asked; Alaia has never told).

**Cross-references:** hook B13 (Rosa Vega named + Berkeley visit), hook B4 (Rosa as warm-long-form former-caster foil; distinct from mid-Act-II single-encounter former-caster), hook A1 (Nia Chen names the network — Rosa must not preempt), hook B1 (Bancroft ledger entry — one of the four remaining). Facts-ledger §2 (Bancroft entry canon), §5 (Alaia lineage), §24 (Rosa canonical entry), §25 (Isabel lineage), §29 (crows misdirection — Rosa is a natural payoff-carrier for the animals-sense-magic seed per T14).

**Never voice at the table before the in-person Berkeley visit:** her former-caster status; her Bancroft ledger role; her specific ex-cast domain; that Alaia is her daughter (unless already surfaced via Vivian). Vivian's Ep 4 characterization ('Isabel's clever daughter who lives in Berkeley') is the public frame; Rosa steps into more only at Ep 6.

**Risk if unresolved:** Rosa is named + pointed-toward with clear urgency in Ep 4 (Vivian: *'If you're serious about my father's work, go and see Rosa.'*). If Ep 6 doesn't route the party to her, Vivian's Ep 4 seed rots and B13 goes overdue. Bake the Berkeley visit into Ep 5-6 planning as a must-fire node.

**Ep 6 addition (2026-08-27 re-shape) — the A3 vehicle.** Mid-conversation Rosa has a small physical moment on the garden slope: a tremor, or a dizziness. Priya does what Priya does, and it eases in a way her clinical training does not account for. **Rosa notices exactly what happened and says nothing** — she has decided not to be the one to tell her. This is the vehicle for Priya's Phase-2 realization (A3), it is delivered PRIVATELY per principles.md §3, and it pays off Priya's covert medical exam of Vivian in Ep 4 (a 98-year-old with a surprisingly strong pulse and a 79-year-old whose tremor stopped make a shape). Rosa's withholding IS the scene, not an obstacle to it.

background.homeBase: A cedar-shingled house in the Berkeley Hills, inherited from Isabel; garden terraced down the slope; a study lined with her own books and her mother's
background.household: Lives alone since her husband died (~2016; a librarian at Cal; kind, uncurious, loved her deeply). Adult daughter Alaia visits most off-weekends from Bodie. A tabby cat named Tomasa who is unimpressed by visitors
background.family: Mother: Isabel Vega (deceased — see isabel-vega.json). Father: Julián Vega (Cal mathematics professor, deceased 1980s; conventional academic, unaware of Isabel's substrate-adjacent correspondence). Husband: unnamed (deceased 2016). Daughter: Alaia Vega (see alaia-vega.json). No other children
background.career: Comparative-literature undergrad at Cal; MLS from San Jose State; cataloguer at Bancroft Library from her late twenties into her sixties; retired ~2013. Her 1979 cataloguing of the 'anomalous ephemera collection' was a private practice inside a public job
background.hobbies: Gardens. Reads in three languages. Adds occasional entries to Ledger 6 when she personally witnesses something. Writes long letters by hand to two old friends she has not seen in twenty years
